274	# Part IV — Layers, transports, and provenance
275	
276	
277	## Occurrences and contents
278	
279	`L169.s1` | FROZEN | An **occurrence** is a physically located carrier.
280	`L169.s2` | FROZEN | A **content** is an organization together with its contract-relative commitments.
281	`L169.s3` | FROZEN | Occurrences are not identified by carrying the same words; contents are not identified by having the same outputs.
282	
283	## The object layer and the simulation layer
284	
285	`L173.s1` | S2 | A modelled thinker has at least two organizations in play.
286	`L175.s1` | S2 | The **object layer** \(P\) is an organization whose ports are persistent things with boundaries and identity, whose components are their continuity relations, and whose admitted edits include displacement, occlusion and re-identification.
287	`L175.s2` | S2 | It is the layer at which there are *objects* rather than a field of sensation.
288	`L177.s1` | FROZEN | The **simulation layer** \(S\) is an organization over \(P\) whose components are dependencies among things and whose queries are predictions: what a port of \(P\) will take under an admitted edit.
289	`L177.s2` | S2 | \(S\) is where prediction lives.
290	`L179.s1` | S2 | Neither layer is presupposed to exist in any particular physical system.
291	`L179.s2` | S2 | The semantics describes what it is for them to exist and to be connected.
292	
293	## Transports
294	
295	`L183.s1` | S2 | A transport from an organization \(D\) to an organization \(E\) is
296	`L185.s1` | FROZEN | \[ t=(\pi,\tau,\sigma,\lambda) \]
297	`L189.s1` | FROZEN | where \(\pi:X_D\to X_E\) on the stated scope, \(\tau\) translates edits, \(\sigma\) translates boundaries, and \(\lambda\) assigns each component of \(E\) a subnetwork of \(D\) with a port translation.
298	`L189.s2` | FROZEN | A transport is **faithful on \(C\)** when it meets the component and global fidelity conditions of Part V.
299	
300	## Three provenances
301	
302	`L193.s1` | S2 | A transport \(t\) whose domain is an organization of a physical system has exactly one of three provenances, determined by its history in the physical module:
303	`L195.s1` | FROZEN | **Selected.** There is a population \(\mathcal T\) of candidate transports, a variation operator \(\mu\) on \(\mathcal T\), a finite history \(H\subseteq C\) of edit–boundary pairs actually encountered, and a survival condition requiring fidelity on \(H\).
304	`L195.s2` | S2 | The transport \(t\) is a member of \(\mathcal T\) that survived.
305	`L195.s3` | S2 | A transport **survives on \(H\)** when it is a member of \(\mathcal T\) that meets the survival condition on \(H\); fidelity on \(H\) without membership in \(\mathcal T\) is not survival.
306	`L195.n4` | S2 | \(\neg[\exists o\prec_{h(t)}o_t,\ x\in\{t,\ H,\ \text{survival condition},\ \operatorname{cod}t\}:\ \operatorname{Rep}(o,x)]\land\neg[\exists h'\subseteq h(t):\ \operatorname{CT}(h',t)]\) (D12.1).
307	`L195.s5` | FROZEN | Write \(\operatorname{Sel}(t;\mathcal T,\mu,H)\).
308	`L195.s6` | S2 | The population \(\mathcal T\) is part of the claim: what \(H\) leaves open about \(t\) is what \(\mathcal T\) leaves open (Argument 3).
309	`L197.s1` | S2 | **Constructed.** There is an episode (Part X) whose construction trace prepares \(t\), and in which \(t\), or the organization it carries to, is available as a represented target.
310	`L197.s2` | S2 | Write \(\operatorname{Con}(t;h,e)\).
311	`L199.s1` | FROZEN | **Declared.** Neither of the above.
312	`L199.s3` | FROZEN | Write \(\operatorname{Dec}(t)\).
313	`L201.s1` | S2 | A physical system may hold selected transports at the object layer and constructed transports at the simulation layer; that is one arrangement, not a requirement.
314	`L201.s2` | FROZEN | Construction may operate on selected material.
315	`L201.s3` | FROZEN | Selection may continue to operate beneath construction.
316	`L201.n4` | S2 | Neither provenance is reducible to the other: (D12.1, D12.2).
317	
318	## Representation is defined, not supplied
319	
320	`L205.s1` | S2 | An occurrence \(o\) **represents** content \(c\) at grain \(\ell\) when there is a transport from the organization that \(o\) instantiates under the physical module, at grain \(\ell\), to \(c\), faithful on \(c\)'s contract, whose provenance is selected or constructed; in (R), \(\operatorname{Sel}(t)\) and \(\operatorname{Con}(t)\) abbreviate \(\operatorname{Sel}(t;\mathcal T,\mu,H)\) and \(\operatorname{Con}(t;h,e)\) for some such parameters:
321	`L207.s1` | FROZEN | \[ \operatorname{Rep}_\ell(o,c)\iff\exists t\,[\operatorname{Faithful}_C(t:\operatorname{Org}_\ell(o)\to c)\land(\operatorname{Sel}(t)\lor\operatorname{Con}(t))]. \tag{R} \]
322	`L211.s1` | S2 | The carrier–content relation is thus a fidelity relation with a history.
323	`L211.s2` | S2 | A system can represent a theory in error: the transport from carrier to content is faithful while the transport from the content's target to the content fails.
324	`L211.s3` | S2 | A declared transport does not make an occurrence represent anything; it makes a modeller assert that it does.
325	`L211.s4` | S2 | A carrier keeps its provenance when present access to it is lost, and a later record made from the carrier carries that provenance, not a second, independent one.
326	`L213.s1` | S2 | The one thing (R) takes from outside is \(\operatorname{Org}_\ell(o)\): which organization a physical occurrence instantiates at a grain.
327	`L213.s2` | S2 | That is supplied by the physical module, not by the semantics.
328	
329	## Prediction, surprise, violation
330	
331	`L217.s1` | S2 | Let \(t\) be a transport to the simulation layer \(S\), with contract \(C\) and, where \(t\) is selected, history \(H\).
332	`L217.s2` | FROZEN | For an edit–boundary pair \((a,b)\in C\) actually occurring:
333	`L219.s1` | FROZEN | - the **prediction** is \(\operatorname{Ans}_S(\tau(a),\sigma(b))\);
334	`L220.n1` | S2 | - a **violation** occurs when \(\neg(\text{F1 at }(a,b)\land\text{F2eq at }(a,b))\) (D12.7);
335	`L221.n1` | S2 | - **surprise** is a violation of a selected transport at \((a,b)\notin H\).
336	`L223.s1` | S2 | A system with no transport cannot be surprised.
337	`L223.s2` | S2 | A system whose history exhausts its contract cannot be surprised.
338	`L223.s3` | S2 | Surprise requires an incomplete selection history: the contract must contain changes the system's correspondence was never shaped against, and one of them must occur (Argument 4).
339	`L223.s4` | S2 | Whether the correspondence could have been otherwise at such a change turns on its population (Argument 3).
340	`L223.n5` | S2 | Prediction and violation are defined for every transport to the simulation layer, surprise only for a selected one: a constructed one that fails at an actually occurring pair of its contract is violated, and the failure is not surprise; a violation the system represents can be a recognized difficulty (Part X).
341	`L225.s1` | FROZEN | Two responses to a violation are distinguished.
342	`L225.s2` | S2 | A **selection response** extends the history \(H\) of a selected transport and lets \(\mu\) act: the transport is re-tuned within the population.
343	`L225.s3` | FROZEN | A **construction response** introduces a new organization or a new transport with a construction trace.
344	`L225.s4` | FROZEN | Only the second can be originative under Part X.
345	
346	# Part V — Account
347	
348	`L231.s1` | S2 | An explanatory candidate for question \(p\) is an organization \(E\), a transport \(t=(\pi,\tau,\sigma,\lambda)\) from \(D\) to \(E\), and an identified set \(\Gamma\) of active commitments in \(E\).
349	`L231.s2` | S2 | The commitments \(\Gamma\) are components of \(E\), those the candidate offers as doing the work, whether or not anyone has described their work; the boundary conditions of \(E\) and the components of \(E\) outside \(\Gamma\), including any of them that assigns an input, belong to the named background of Part VI.
350	`L231.s3` | S2 | The candidate together with its question, \(\mathcal E=(E,p,t,\Gamma)\), meets \(\operatorname{Account}(\mathcal E)\) exactly when the following four conditions are met, each a condition on supplied relations under the changes in \(C\).
351	`L231.s4` | S2 | Where an organization \(E'\) is obtained from \(E\) by a declared operation (Part VI), \(\operatorname{Account}(E',p)\) abbreviates \(\operatorname{Account}\big((E',p,t',\Gamma')\big)\), with \(t'\) the transport the operation carries \(t\) to and \(\Gamma'\) the commitments it leaves; for \(E|W\), \(t'\) is \(t\) with \(\lambda\) restricted to the components of \(E|W\), and \(\Gamma'\) is \(W\).
352	`L233.s1` | S2 | **Component fidelity.** For every active component \(k\) of \(E\) with counterpart subnetwork \(\lambda(k)\subseteq D\), and every \((a,b)\in C\), the relation obtained by imposing the constraints of \(\lambda(k)\), projecting away its hidden ports and carrying what remains to \(V_k\) by the port translation of \(\lambda\) (write \(\operatorname{proj}^{\lambda}_{V_k}\) for this projection) equals the component relation of \(k\) under the translated edit:
353	`L235.s1` | S2 | \[ \operatorname{proj}^{\lambda}_{V_k}\!\big[\operatorname{Sol}_{\lambda(k)}(a,b)\big]=L_k(\tau(a),\sigma(b)). \tag{F1} \]
354	`L239.s1` | S2 | And the assembled organization agrees:
355	`L241.s1` | FROZEN | \[ \pi[\operatorname{Sol}_D(a,b)]=\operatorname{Sol}_E(\tau(a),\sigma(b)),\qquad \tau(1)=1,\quad \tau(a_2a_1)=\tau(a_2)\tau(a_1). \tag{F2} \]
356	`L245.s1` | FROZEN | (F1) prevents an assembled match from hiding a decomposition in error.
357	`L245.s2` | FROZEN | (F2) prevents a set of pieces each faithful locally from hiding a lost shared constraint.
358	`L245.s3` | FROZEN | Together they are fidelity at every level the contract reaches.
359	`L245.s4` | S2 | By (K), no component of \(E\) whose signature on \(C\) differs from its counterpart's meets (F1); there is no further condition about kinds to state (Argument 1).
360	`L247.s1` | FROZEN | **Question fidelity.** For every \((a,b)\in C\),
361	`L249.s1` | FROZEN | \[ \operatorname{Ans}_E(\tau(a),\sigma(b))=\operatorname{Ans}_p(a,b). \tag{A} \]
362	`L253.s1` | FROZEN | The query \(\mathcal Q\) is held fixed; an account of a different query is not an account of this one.
363	`L255.n1` | S2 | **\(\operatorname{Dependence}\).** The answer follows by evaluating \(E\) under its boundary conditions.
364	`L255.n2` | S2 | There exist \((a,b)\in C\) and a nonempty block \(G\subseteq\Gamma\) such that \(\operatorname{Ans}_E(\tau(a),\sigma(b))\neq\operatorname{Ans}_E(1,\sigma(b_0))\) (D6.4), and this contrast is lost when the components of \(G\) are deleted from \(E\) (a deleted component imposes the full relation on its ports, Part II): evaluated at \((\tau(a),\sigma(b))\) and at \((1,\sigma(b_0))\), the answers of \(E\) with \(G\) deleted are determined and equal, or an answer that \(E\) determines at one of these points is not determined there once \(G\) is deleted.
365	`L257.s1` | S2 | **Non-vacuity.** \(\operatorname{Sol}_D(1,b_0)\neq\varnothing\).
366	`L257.n2` | S2 | \(C\subseteq A\times B\) and \((A\times B)\setminus C\subseteq\operatorname{Excl}(\Sigma)\) (D3.5).
367	`L257.n3` | S2 | A contract consisting only of relabelings (D6.9), or excluding every change under which the active commitments could matter to \(\mathcal Q\), admits no candidate that meets (F2), (A) and \(\operatorname{Dependence}\) (FC21), and is therefore not a contract on which an account can be claimed.
368	`L259.s1` | S2 | Thus
369	`L261.n1` | S2 | \[ \operatorname{Account}(\mathcal E)\iff \text{(F1)}\land\text{(F2)}\land\text{(A)}\land\text{Dependence}\land\text{NonVacuous}. \tag{E} \]
370	`L265.n1` | S2 | Every conjunct but \(\operatorname{Stated}(C,\Sigma)\) (D3.5, D6.6) is a condition on how supplied relations behave under the changes in \(C\).
371	`L265.s2` | FROZEN | None inspects a label.
372	
373	## What (E) excludes, and what it does not
374	
375	`L269.n1` | S2 | A **table of observed answers** has no component whose relation is replaced by an intervention; it fails (F1) under \(C\) when \((1,b),(a,b)\in C\) and \(\operatorname{proj}^{\lambda}_{V_k}[\operatorname{Sol}_{\lambda(k)}(a,b)]\neq\operatorname{proj}^{\lambda}_{V_k}[\operatorname{Sol}_{\lambda(k)}(1,b)]\) for a component \(k\) of it (FC25).
376	`L269.s2` | S2 | A table that encodes an organization's response to every admitted change is not a table in that sense: it meets (F1) as a decomposition does, and it is an account when it meets the other conjuncts of (E).
377	`L269.s3` | S2 | The word "table" fixes nothing; the response under the admitted changes does.
378	`L271.s1` | S2 | A **reversed calculation**, identification presented as production, fails (F2) under the production contract: intervening on the upstream port changes the target's downstream value but not the calculation's.
379	`L271.s2` | S2 | It may be faithful under the identification contract, which is a different question (Part III).
380	`L273.n1` | S2 | (D6.3, FC23, FC24).
381	`L275.n1` | S2 | A candidate whose only substantive contrast is one that no edit the target admits realizes has no pair of \(C\) at which the contrast appears, and fails \(\operatorname{Dependence}\).
382	`L275.s2` | S2 | A contrast that no one could produce, or that could not come about, is still a contrast of its question when the target admits the edit that realizes it; whether it can be produced bears on testing (Part XII), not on (E).
383	`L277.s1` | S2 | (E) has no condition on how a mechanism came to be guessed: a mechanism meets (E) or fails it whatever led anyone to guess it, and how it came to be taken up is assessed elsewhere (Part IX).
384	`L277.s2` | S2 | It draws no line between two candidates with the same fidelity that differ only in elegance: both meet it or both fail it.
385	`L277.s3` | S2 | It does not exclude a coarse dependence for omitting finer workings or an instrument: an account at a coarse grain is an account of the coarse question, and what it answers is fixed by its contract, not by what a finer contract would add.
386	`L277.s4` | S2 | A mathematical argument answering "why does this follow under these rules?" meets (E) for that question without answering "what caused this?"; depth is question-relative and (E) measures none of it.
387	
388	## Why there is no counterpart-kind condition
389	
390	`L281.s1` | S2 | A separate condition, "each component of \(E\) must be tied to a component of \(D\) *of the same kind*", would be either redundant or unevaluable.
391	`L281.s2` | S2 | Where \(C\) contains a change separating two kinds, (F1) already fails for a component whose counterpart is of the other kind.
392	`L281.s3` | FROZEN | Where \(C\) contains no such change, the two are one kind on \(C\) by (K), and the condition would be asserting a distinction that \(C\) does not contain.
393	`L281.s4` | FROZEN | There is no third case.
394	`L281.s5` | S2 | Argument 1 makes this exact.
395	
396	# Part VI — Work, routes, and interference
397	
398	`L287.s1` | FROZEN | Fix \(\mathcal E\) and a declared restriction operation.
399	`L287.s2` | S2 | For \(W\subseteq\Gamma\), let \(E|W\) retain the commitments in \(W\) with the named background fixed; the commitments of \(E|W\) are \(W\).
400	`L287.s3` | S2 | Define
401	`L289.s1` | FROZEN | \[ \mathsf S_{E,p}=\{W\subseteq\Gamma:\operatorname{Account}(E|W,p)\}. \tag{S} \]
402	`L293.s1` | FROZEN | No upward closure and no minimal member are assumed.
403	`L293.s2` | S2 | For nonempty \(B\subseteq W\),
404	`L295.s1` | FROZEN | \[ \operatorname{CriticalBlock}(B;W,p)\iff W\in\mathsf S_{E,p}\land W\setminus B\notin\mathsf S_{E,p}. \tag{B} \]
405	`L299.s1` | FROZEN | A block may be critical while no singleton in it is.
406	`L299.s2` | S2 | Criticality is relative to the route \(W\) it is assessed in, a **route** of the candidate being a member of \(\mathsf S_{E,p}\) (not an active route of a history, Part IX): a commitment critical in one route need not be critical in the full candidate, and the routes assessed are subsets of the written \(\Gamma\), whether or not anyone has set them out, not a route someone could write with commitments outside \(\Gamma\).
407	`L299.s3` | S2 | For a declared family \(\mathcal V\) of organization edits,
408	`L301.s1` | FROZEN | \[ \operatorname{Boundary}_{E,p}=\{(v,w)\in\mathcal V^2:\operatorname{Account}(E_v,p)\neq\operatorname{Account}(E_w,p)\}. \tag{D} \]
409	`L305.s1` | S2 | **Finite monotone claim.** If \(\Gamma\) is finite, \(\mathsf S\) is upward closed, and \(\Gamma\in\mathsf S\), then \(d\in\Gamma\) is critical for some route (**contributory**) exactly when \(d\in\bigcup\min\mathsf S\), and \(d\) is **globally indispensable**, \(\Gamma\setminus\{d\}\notin\mathsf S_{E,p}\), exactly when \(d\in\bigcap\min\mathsf S\).
410	`L305.s2` | S2 | *Why this and not its denial.*
411	`L305.s3` | S2 | A member of a minimal route is critical for it.
412	`L305.s4` | S2 | If \(d\) is critical for \(W\), finiteness gives a minimal \(U\subseteq W\); if \(d\notin U\), upward closure makes \(W\setminus\{d\}\) a route.
413	`L305.s5` | S2 | Deletion of \(d\) from \(\Gamma\) leaves \(\Gamma\setminus\{d\}\) a route exactly when a minimal route omits \(d\). ∎ The claim applies only where its assumptions are met; an addition to \(\Gamma\) that stops a route being one is the interference case below, and there upward closure fails.
414	`L307.s1` | FROZEN | **Redundant routes.** \(\Gamma=\{a,b\}\), \(\mathsf S=\{\{a\},\{b\},\{a,b\}\}\): each is contributory, neither indispensable.
415	`L307.s2` | S2 | Two systems with the same output table may differ in which routes are active; the semantics represents the difference (Argument 9).
416	`L307.s3` | S2 | A route of the candidate is a route whether or not any history runs it; it is active in a system when occurrences that realize it form an active route (Part IX), a subnetwork of actual occurrences in the system's history.
417	`L307.s4` | S2 | The two meet in \(\operatorname{ProducedBy}\) (Part XI), which attributes a repair to the contributions whose active routes ran to it, not to the routes a candidate contains.
418	`L307.s5` | S2 | A route already present in the candidate is a route whether or not anyone has described its work; a component reassigned to a new target after a deletion belongs to a new candidate with its own assessment, and whether the new candidate meets (E) is not whether the old one does.
419	`L309.s1` | FROZEN | **Interference.** \(\Gamma=\{a,b\}\), \(\mathsf S=\{\{a\}\}\): the full candidate fails (E) although a subset meets it.
420	`L309.s2` | S2 | A subset can meet (E) while the whole fails it; \(b\) is not made "not a commitment" to repair this.
421	`L311.s1` | S2 | **Infinitary routes.** \(\Gamma=\{d_n:n\in\mathbb N\}\), \(d_n\) the constraint \(|x|\le 1/n\): every set of indices unbounded in \(\mathbb N\) determines \(x=0\); no minimal route, and no route of one commitment, exists.
422	`L311.s2` | FROZEN | (B) records the collective contribution.
423	`L313.s1` | S2 | **Commitments that do no work.** (E) has no condition that each commitment do work.
424	`L313.s2` | S2 | A commitment \(d\) of a candidate that has a route does no work by itself in it when every route stays a route after \(d\) is added to it and after \(d\) is removed from it: a candidate carrying \(d\) then meets (E) exactly when it meets (E) without \(d\), and \(\{d\}\) is critical in no route (B).
425	`L313.n3` | S2 | When \(\Gamma\) is infinite, a block of such commitments can still be critical (Infinitary routes; FC40 (c)).
426	`L315.s1` | FROZEN | **Rivals.** Two explanatory candidates for one question \(p\) are **rivals** when one of them has been offered as an answer to \(p\) in place of the other and they conflict at some admitted edit–boundary pair of the target that both their transports translate, in \(C\) or outside it.
427	`L315.n2` | S2 | Two candidates **conflict** at such a pair \((a,b)\) when their answers there differ (D8.2), or when each of them could meet (F1), (F2) and (A) there under some relations of the target's components at that pair, each a relation on the component's footprint (Part II), and no such relations let both, as none do when two of their active components with one counterpart have different relations there (D8.new1).
428	`L315.s3` | S2 | Whether two candidates conflict depends on their organizations and transports and on the target's ports and components, not on anyone's view of them; it is found by argument, with no test, and it does not turn on what any physics admits (Part I).
429	`L315.s4` | FROZEN | A candidate offered for \(p\) is offered for the whole of \(p\): it claims (F1), (F2) and (A) at every pair of \(C\), tested or not, and the rest of (E) on \(C\); outside \(C\) it claims nothing on \(p\), but what its organization and transport give there can conflict with what another's give.
430	`L315.s5` | FROZEN | Two candidates that differ only in how they are written, one carried onto the other by a structure-preserving bijection that takes its transport with it and leaves its answers as they are, conflict at no pair (Part VIII, Recoding; Argument 8), and nor do two candidates, however differently they are cut, that some such relations of the target would let both meet (F1), (F2) and (A) at each admitted pair both translate; neither pair is a pair of rivals.
431	`L315.s6` | S2 | A claim is **ruled out** for an assessor \(j\) when an argument usable by \(j\) (Part IX) rules it out, and a candidate is ruled out for \(j\) when the claim that it meets (E) is; by (K3), an argument from a test's record rules out a candidate only together with the background and instruments of that test.
432	`L315.s7` | FROZEN | A candidate is **not ruled out** for \(j\) when no argument usable by \(j\) rules it out.
433	`L315.s8` | FROZEN | No list of all rivals is supposed: a candidate's rivals are among the candidates someone has offered, and a candidate that nobody has offered is no one's rival.
434	`L315.s9` | S2 | Nor are rivals a selection population: whether a selected transport is underdetermined at an unseen pair is fixed by its population (Argument 3), whatever rivals anyone offers.
435	`L315.s10` | FROZEN | **Conflict with a claim.** A candidate can conflict with a claim as well as with a rival.
436	`L315.n11` | S2 | A candidate **conflicts with** a claim \(\chi\) at an admitted pair of the target that its transport translates, in \(C\) or outside it, when \(\chi\) excludes what the candidate's organization and transport give there: its answer, or every relation of the target's components under which it could meet (F1), (F2) and (A) there (D8.5).
437	`L315.s12` | S2 | \(\chi\) need not be an explanation or come with one, and it may be a claim about what is possible or impossible: the bare claim that perpetual motion is impossible is enough for a conflict with a candidate whose organization gives perpetual motion.
438	`L315.s13` | S2 | Such a conflict is found by argument, with no test against the target: an argument that rules out, for whoever can use it, that what the candidate gives there is something \(\chi\) allows (Part IX).
439	`L315.s14` | S2 | Where the pair is in \(C\), that argument rules out that the candidate meets (E) for any assessor \(j\) who can use it, and so who tentatively accepts \(\chi\) (K2); outside \(C\) it rules out that the target gives there what the candidate's organization gives, not the candidate's meeting (E) on \(p\).
440	`L315.s15` | S2 | Either way the argument needs the premise that \(\chi\) speaks of the target under that pair's edit.
441	`L315.s16` | S2 | Where the edit is itself one that \(\chi\) excludes, as when a question asks what a pendulum does with its friction component deleted, the target so edited may itself give a motion that never stops, and without that premise the argument rules out no candidate there; the candidate still conflicts with \(\chi\).
442	`L315.s17` | FROZEN | The conflict does not by itself say which to drop, the candidate, \(\chi\) or another premise of the argument: which one the person goes on with is the person's choice (Part 0), and using \(\chi\) as a premise gives \(\chi\) nothing.
443	`L315.n18` | S2 | Nor is the conflict enough to do anything about it: ruling the candidate out by \(\chi\) is already doing something about it, and is a choice the person made in taking \(\chi\) as given, not something \(\chi\) does by itself; a response that changes the candidate, the claim or the question is construction and repair (Parts X, XI); and \(\chi\) alone does not say where the candidate is in error.
444	`L315.s19` | S2 | A conflict with a claim that a system represents can be a recognized difficulty (Part X), as when keeping the candidate meets a claimed aim only by dropping the claim, where keeping the claim is among the protected aims (Part XI).
445	`L315.s20` | S2 | Two candidates that some relations of the target's components would let both meet (F1), (F2) and (A) at a pair, when \(\chi\) excludes every such relation, conflict there given \(\chi\): an argument that rules out their both meeting (F1), (F2) and (A) there uses \(\chi\) as a premise and lapses with it.
446	`L315.s21` | S2 | Two candidates offered one in place of the other that conflict at a pair given \(\chi\) are **rivals given \(\chi\)**: for an assessor who tentatively accepts \(\chi\) they pose a problem for \(p\) as rivals do (Problems, below), and for one who does not, they pose none on that account.
447	`L317.s1` | FROZEN | **Problems.** Two rivals, neither of them ruled out for an assessor, pose, for that assessor, a **problem for \(p\)**: a conflict between ideas that no argument usable by that assessor has decided.
448	`L317.s2` | FROZEN | It is of one of two kinds.
449	`L317.s3` | FROZEN | (i) The rivals conflict at some \((a,b)\in C\).
450	`L317.n4` | S2 | Whatever the target does there, at most one of them is an account of \(p\), whether or not anyone records what it does; recording it (D10.3) is a **test**.
451	`L317.s5` | S2 | Whatever it records, an argument from what it records rules out at least one of them for an assessor who can use it, that is, for whom its steps' forms are admitted, its scope is the one declared and its premises about the test's background and instruments are live (K2, K3), while it stays usable; taking those premises as given is that assessor's choice, and so is the ruling out that uses them, which the test does not make by itself (Part 0); an answer that such an argument rules out stays ruled out on \(p\) for as long as the argument stays usable (Part VIII).
452	`L317.s6` | FROZEN | (ii) They conflict at no pair of \(C\), only at admitted pairs outside it: the contract does not contain their conflict.
453	`L317.s7` | S2 | Their answers then agree at every pair of \(C\), so no argument from an answer recorded in \(C\) rules out one of them without the other; an argument from a test inside \(C\) can rule out one of them without the other only for a failure of its own; and where both meet (E) on \(C\) both are accounts of \(p\).
454	`L317.n8` | S2 | Either kind of problem can also be solved with no test, by an argument usable by that assessor that rules out that one of the rivals meets (E) on \(C\): one that finds, by examining it, that at a pair of \(C\) it gives what a claim the assessor tentatively accepts excludes (conflict with a claim, above; Part IX).
455	`L317.s9` | S2 | Solving a problem so rules one rival out for that assessor while the argument stays usable for that assessor.
456	`L317.s10` | S2 | Where the argument uses a claim the assessor tentatively accepts, that ruling out is a choice the assessor made, in taking the claim as given and going on with it, and not something the claim does by itself; it is already something done about the conflict with the claim, which does not say where the rival is in error, and what the person goes on with stays the person's choice (conflict with a claim, above).
457	`L317.n11` | S2 | A candidate is **easy to vary** (D10.4), in the sense used here, when it and a rival pose a problem of the second kind; the rival is then easy to vary too, and the term says nothing about which of them, and not the other, is an account on a finer contract.
458	`L317.s12` | FROZEN | A criticism that a candidate is easy to vary must supply such a rival (Part IX).
459	`L317.s13` | S2 | Two rivals that are both accounts on \(C\) conflict only outside it, and a claim that one of them and not the other meets (E) on a contract with some admitted change outside \(C\) is a claim that such a change separates them, and must supply it, as a claim that the target pairs its components one way and not the other must (Argument 2, Consequence).
460	`L317.n14` | S2 | A finer contract that contains a change at which two rivals conflict makes a new question (Part III), on which, offered for it, they pose a problem of the first kind while neither is ruled out; whether a candidate is an account of a question depends on the candidate, the question and its target, and not on anyone's view of them, on when anyone first asks the question or on whether anyone has tested the candidate on it (Parts I and V); nothing about it is ever settled, and whatever anyone accepts about it, that a candidate is an account or that it is not, is accepted tentatively (Part 0).
461	`L317.s15` | FROZEN | A contract narrowed to leave out the pairs at which two rivals conflict also makes a different question; it solves nothing on \(p\), and the problem for \(p\) remains until at least one of them is ruled out for that assessor.
462	`L317.s16` | S2 | Nothing here counts rivals or orders candidates: of one candidate, what is said is whether it meets (E) on a contract and whether it is ruled out for an assessor; of two, whether they conflict; of a candidate and a claim, whether they conflict.
463	`L317.s17` | FROZEN | A problem that a system represents can be a recognized difficulty (Part X), as when choosing one of two rivals meets a claimed aim only by dropping the other, which is not ruled out either, where keeping every rival not ruled out is among the protected aims (Part XI).
464	
465	# Part VII — Exact constructions
466	
467	
468	## Production and direction
469	
470	`L325.s1` | S2 | Stipulate \(H:=U_H,\ \theta:=U_\theta,\ L:=H\cot\theta\), where \(U_H\) and \(U_\theta\) are exogenous values setting the pole's height \(H\) and the sun's elevation \(\theta\), and \(L\) is the length of the pole's shadow.
471	`L325.s2` | S2 | Under \(A\) containing interventions on \(H\) and \(\theta\), these ports are inputs and \(L\) is an output, by Part II.

# Part IV — Layers, transports, and provenance


## Occurrences and contents

`L169.s1` | FROZEN | An **occurrence** is a physically located carrier.
`L169.s2` | FROZEN | A **content** is an organization together with its contract-relative commitments.
`L169.s3` | FROZEN | Occurrences are not identified by carrying the same words; contents are not identified by having the same outputs.

## The object layer and the simulation layer

`L173.s1` | S2 | A modelled thinker has at least two organizations in play.
`L175.s1` | S2 | The **object layer** \(P\) is an organization whose ports are persistent things with boundaries and identity, whose components are their continuity relations, and whose admitted edits include displacement, occlusion and re-identification.
`L175.s2` | S2 | It is the layer at which there are *objects* rather than a field of sensation.
`L177.s1` | FROZEN | The **simulation layer** \(S\) is an organization over \(P\) whose components are dependencies among things and whose queries are predictions: what a port of \(P\) will take under an admitted edit.
`L177.s2` | S2 | \(S\) is where prediction lives.
`L179.s1` | S2 | Neither layer is presupposed to exist in any particular physical system.
`L179.s2` | S2 | The semantics describes what it is for them to exist and to be connected.

## Transports

`L183.s1` | S2 | A transport from an organization \(D\) to an organization \(E\) is
`L185.s1` | FROZEN | \[ t=(\pi,\tau,\sigma,\lambda) \]
`L189.s1` | FROZEN | where \(\pi:X_D\to X_E\) on the stated scope, \(\tau\) translates edits, \(\sigma\) translates boundaries, and \(\lambda\) assigns each component of \(E\) a subnetwork of \(D\) with a port translation.
`L189.s2` | FROZEN | A transport is **faithful on \(C\)** when it meets the component and global fidelity conditions of Part V.

## Three provenances

`L193.s1` | S2 | A transport \(t\) whose domain is an organization of a physical system has exactly one of three provenances, determined by its history in the physical module:
`L195.s1` | FROZEN | **Selected.** There is a population \(\mathcal T\) of candidate transports, a variation operator \(\mu\) on \(\mathcal T\), a finite history \(H\subseteq C\) of edit–boundary pairs actually encountered, and a survival condition requiring fidelity on \(H\).
`L195.s2` | S2 | The transport \(t\) is a member of \(\mathcal T\) that survived.
`L195.s3` | S2 | A transport **survives on \(H\)** when it is a member of \(\mathcal T\) that meets the survival condition on \(H\); fidelity on \(H\) without membership in \(\mathcal T\) is not survival.
`L195.n4` | S2 | \(\neg[\exists o\prec_{h(t)}o_t,\ x\in\{t,\ H,\ \text{survival condition},\ \operatorname{cod}t\}:\ \operatorname{Rep}(o,x)]\land\neg[\exists h'\subseteq h(t):\ \operatorname{CT}(h',t)]\) (D12.1).
`L195.s5` | FROZEN | Write \(\operatorname{Sel}(t;\mathcal T,\mu,H)\).
`L195.s6` | S2 | The population \(\mathcal T\) is part of the claim: what \(H\) leaves open about \(t\) is what \(\mathcal T\) leaves open (Argument 3).
`L197.s1` | S2 | **Constructed.** There is an episode (Part X) whose construction trace prepares \(t\), and in which \(t\), or the organization it carries to, is available as a represented target.
`L197.s2` | S2 | Write \(\operatorname{Con}(t;h,e)\).
`L199.s1` | FROZEN | **Declared.** Neither of the above.
`L199.s3` | FROZEN | Write \(\operatorname{Dec}(t)\).
`L201.s1` | S2 | A physical system may hold selected transports at the object layer and constructed transports at the simulation layer; that is one arrangement, not a requirement.
`L201.s2` | FROZEN | Construction may operate on selected material.
`L201.s3` | FROZEN | Selection may continue to operate beneath construction.
`L201.n4` | S2 | Neither provenance is reducible to the other: (D12.1, D12.2).

## Representation is defined, not supplied

`L205.s1` | S2 | An occurrence \(o\) **represents** content \(c\) at grain \(\ell\) when there is a transport from the organization that \(o\) instantiates under the physical module, at grain \(\ell\), to \(c\), faithful on \(c\)'s contract, whose provenance is selected or constructed; in (R), \(\operatorname{Sel}(t)\) and \(\operatorname{Con}(t)\) abbreviate \(\operatorname{Sel}(t;\mathcal T,\mu,H)\) and \(\operatorname{Con}(t;h,e)\) for some such parameters:
`L207.s1` | FROZEN | \[ \operatorname{Rep}_\ell(o,c)\iff\exists t\,[\operatorname{Faithful}_C(t:\operatorname{Org}_\ell(o)\to c)\land(\operatorname{Sel}(t)\lor\operatorname{Con}(t))]. \tag{R} \]
`L211.s1` | S2 | The carrier–content relation is thus a fidelity relation with a history.
`L211.s2` | S2 | A system can represent a theory in error: the transport from carrier to content is faithful while the transport from the content's target to the content fails.
`L211.s3` | S2 | A declared transport does not make an occurrence represent anything; it makes a modeller assert that it does.
`L211.s4` | S2 | A carrier keeps its provenance when present access to it is lost, and a later record made from the carrier carries that provenance, not a second, independent one.
`L213.s1` | S2 | The one thing (R) takes from outside is \(\operatorname{Org}_\ell(o)\): which organization a physical occurrence instantiates at a grain.
`L213.s2` | S2 | That is supplied by the physical module, not by the semantics.

## Prediction, surprise, violation

`L217.s1` | S2 | Let \(t\) be a transport to the simulation layer \(S\), with contract \(C\) and, where \(t\) is selected, history \(H\).
`L217.s2` | FROZEN | For an edit–boundary pair \((a,b)\in C\) actually occurring:
`L219.s1` | FROZEN | - the **prediction** is \(\operatorname{Ans}_S(\tau(a),\sigma(b))\);
`L220.n1` | S2 | - a **violation** occurs when \(\neg(\text{F1 at }(a,b)\land\text{F2eq at }(a,b))\) (D12.7);
`L221.n1` | S2 | - **surprise** is a violation of a selected transport at \((a,b)\notin H\).
`L223.s1` | S2 | A system with no transport cannot be surprised.
`L223.s2` | S2 | A system whose history exhausts its contract cannot be surprised.
`L223.s3` | S2 | Surprise requires an incomplete selection history: the contract must contain changes the system's correspondence was never shaped against, and one of them must occur (Argument 4).
`L223.s4` | S2 | Whether the correspondence could have been otherwise at such a change turns on its population (Argument 3).
`L223.n5` | S2 | Prediction and violation are defined for every transport to the simulation layer, surprise only for a selected one: a constructed one that fails at an actually occurring pair of its contract is violated, and the failure is not surprise; a violation the system represents can be a recognized difficulty (Part X).
`L225.s1` | FROZEN | Two responses to a violation are distinguished.
`L225.s2` | S2 | A **selection response** extends the history \(H\) of a selected transport and lets \(\mu\) act: the transport is re-tuned within the population.
`L225.s3` | FROZEN | A **construction response** introduces a new organization or a new transport with a construction trace.
`L225.s4` | FROZEN | Only the second can be originative under Part X.

# Part V — Account

`L231.s1` | S2 | An explanatory candidate for question \(p\) is an organization \(E\), a transport \(t=(\pi,\tau,\sigma,\lambda)\) from \(D\) to \(E\), and an identified set \(\Gamma\) of active commitments in \(E\).
`L231.s2` | S2 | The commitments \(\Gamma\) are components of \(E\), those the candidate offers as doing the work, whether or not anyone has described their work; the boundary conditions of \(E\) and the components of \(E\) outside \(\Gamma\), including any of them that assigns an input, belong to the named background of Part VI.
`L231.s3` | S2 | The candidate together with its question, \(\mathcal E=(E,p,t,\Gamma)\), meets \(\operatorname{Account}(\mathcal E)\) exactly when the following four conditions are met, each a condition on supplied relations under the changes in \(C\).
`L231.s4` | S2 | Where an organization \(E'\) is obtained from \(E\) by a declared operation (Part VI), \(\operatorname{Account}(E',p)\) abbreviates \(\operatorname{Account}\big((E',p,t',\Gamma')\big)\), with \(t'\) the transport the operation carries \(t\) to and \(\Gamma'\) the commitments it leaves; for \(E|W\), \(t'\) is \(t\) with \(\lambda\) restricted to the components of \(E|W\), and \(\Gamma'\) is \(W\).
`L233.s1` | S2 | **Component fidelity.** For every active component \(k\) of \(E\) with counterpart subnetwork \(\lambda(k)\subseteq D\), and every \((a,b)\in C\), the relation obtained by imposing the constraints of \(\lambda(k)\), projecting away its hidden ports and carrying what remains to \(V_k\) by the port translation of \(\lambda\) (write \(\operatorname{proj}^{\lambda}_{V_k}\) for this projection) equals the component relation of \(k\) under the translated edit:
`L235.s1` | S2 | \[ \operatorname{proj}^{\lambda}_{V_k}\!\big[\operatorname{Sol}_{\lambda(k)}(a,b)\big]=L_k(\tau(a),\sigma(b)). \tag{F1} \]
`L239.s1` | S2 | And the assembled organization agrees:
`L241.s1` | FROZEN | \[ \pi[\operatorname{Sol}_D(a,b)]=\operatorname{Sol}_E(\tau(a),\sigma(b)),\qquad \tau(1)=1,\quad \tau(a_2a_1)=\tau(a_2)\tau(a_1). \tag{F2} \]
`L245.s1` | FROZEN | (F1) prevents an assembled match from hiding a decomposition in error.
`L245.s2` | FROZEN | (F2) prevents a set of pieces each faithful locally from hiding a lost shared constraint.
`L245.s3` | FROZEN | Together they are fidelity at every level the contract reaches.
`L245.s4` | S2 | By (K), no component of \(E\) whose signature on \(C\) differs from its counterpart's meets (F1); there is no further condition about kinds to state (Argument 1).
`L247.s1` | FROZEN | **Question fidelity.** For every \((a,b)\in C\),
`L249.s1` | FROZEN | \[ \operatorname{Ans}_E(\tau(a),\sigma(b))=\operatorname{Ans}_p(a,b). \tag{A} \]
`L253.s1` | FROZEN | The query \(\mathcal Q\) is held fixed; an account of a different query is not an account of this one.
`L255.n1` | S2 | **\(\operatorname{Dependence}\).** The answer follows by evaluating \(E\) under its boundary conditions.
`L255.n2` | S2 | There exist \((a,b)\in C\) and a nonempty block \(G\subseteq\Gamma\) such that \(\operatorname{Ans}_E(\tau(a),\sigma(b))\neq\operatorname{Ans}_E(1,\sigma(b_0))\) (D6.4), and this contrast is lost when the components of \(G\) are deleted from \(E\) (a deleted component imposes the full relation on its ports, Part II): evaluated at \((\tau(a),\sigma(b))\) and at \((1,\sigma(b_0))\), the answers of \(E\) with \(G\) deleted are determined and equal, or an answer that \(E\) determines at one of these points is not determined there once \(G\) is deleted.
`L257.s1` | S2 | **Non-vacuity.** \(\operatorname{Sol}_D(1,b_0)\neq\varnothing\).
`L257.n2` | S2 | \(C\subseteq A\times B\) and \((A\times B)\setminus C\subseteq\operatorname{Excl}(\Sigma)\) (D3.5).
`L257.n3` | S2 | A contract consisting only of relabelings (D6.9), or excluding every change under which the active commitments could matter to \(\mathcal Q\), admits no candidate that meets (F2), (A) and \(\operatorname{Dependence}\) (FC21), and is therefore not a contract on which an account can be claimed.
`L259.s1` | S2 | Thus
`L261.n1` | S2 | \[ \operatorname{Account}(\mathcal E)\iff \text{(F1)}\land\text{(F2)}\land\text{(A)}\land\text{Dependence}\land\text{NonVacuous}. \tag{E} \]
`L265.n1` | S2 | Every conjunct but \(\operatorname{Stated}(C,\Sigma)\) (D3.5, D6.6) is a condition on how supplied relations behave under the changes in \(C\).
`L265.s2` | FROZEN | None inspects a label.

## What (E) excludes, and what it does not

`L269.n1` | S2 | A **table of observed answers** has no component whose relation is replaced by an intervention; it fails (F1) under \(C\) when \((1,b),(a,b)\in C\) and \(\operatorname{proj}^{\lambda}_{V_k}[\operatorname{Sol}_{\lambda(k)}(a,b)]\neq\operatorname{proj}^{\lambda}_{V_k}[\operatorname{Sol}_{\lambda(k)}(1,b)]\) for a component \(k\) of it (FC25).
`L269.s2` | S2 | A table that encodes an organization's response to every admitted change is not a table in that sense: it meets (F1) as a decomposition does, and it is an account when it meets the other conjuncts of (E).
`L269.s3` | S2 | The word "table" fixes nothing; the response under the admitted changes does.
`L271.s1` | S2 | A **reversed calculation**, identification presented as production, fails (F2) under the production contract: intervening on the upstream port changes the target's downstream value but not the calculation's.
`L271.s2` | S2 | It may be faithful under the identification contract, which is a different question (Part III).
`L273.n1` | S2 | (D6.3, FC23, FC24).
`L275.n1` | S2 | A candidate whose only substantive contrast is one that no edit the target admits realizes has no pair of \(C\) at which the contrast appears, and fails \(\operatorname{Dependence}\).
`L275.s2` | S2 | A contrast that no one could produce, or that could not come about, is still a contrast of its question when the target admits the edit that realizes it; whether it can be produced bears on testing (Part XII), not on (E).
`L277.s1` | S2 | (E) has no condition on how a mechanism came to be guessed: a mechanism meets (E) or fails it whatever led anyone to guess it, and how it came to be taken up is assessed elsewhere (Part IX).
`L277.s2` | S2 | It draws no line between two candidates with the same fidelity that differ only in elegance: both meet it or both fail it.
`L277.s3` | S2 | It does not exclude a coarse dependence for omitting finer workings or an instrument: an account at a coarse grain is an account of the coarse question, and what it answers is fixed by its contract, not by what a finer contract would add.
`L277.s4` | S2 | A mathematical argument answering "why does this follow under these rules?" meets (E) for that question without answering "what caused this?"; depth is question-relative and (E) measures none of it.

## Why there is no counterpart-kind condition

`L281.s1` | S2 | A separate condition, "each component of \(E\) must be tied to a component of \(D\) *of the same kind*", would be either redundant or unevaluable.
`L281.s2` | S2 | Where \(C\) contains a change separating two kinds, (F1) already fails for a component whose counterpart is of the other kind.
`L281.s3` | FROZEN | Where \(C\) contains no such change, the two are one kind on \(C\) by (K), and the condition would be asserting a distinction that \(C\) does not contain.
`L281.s4` | FROZEN | There is no third case.
`L281.s5` | S2 | Argument 1 makes this exact.

# Part VI — Work, routes, and interference

`L287.s1` | FROZEN | Fix \(\mathcal E\) and a declared restriction operation.
`L287.s2` | S2 | For \(W\subseteq\Gamma\), let \(E|W\) retain the commitments in \(W\) with the named background fixed; the commitments of \(E|W\) are \(W\).
`L287.s3` | S2 | Define
`L289.s1` | FROZEN | \[ \mathsf S_{E,p}=\{W\subseteq\Gamma:\operatorname{Account}(E|W,p)\}. \tag{S} \]
`L293.s1` | FROZEN | No upward closure and no minimal member are assumed.
`L293.s2` | S2 | For nonempty \(B\subseteq W\),
`L295.s1` | FROZEN | \[ \operatorname{CriticalBlock}(B;W,p)\iff W\in\mathsf S_{E,p}\land W\setminus B\notin\mathsf S_{E,p}. \tag{B} \]
`L299.s1` | FROZEN | A block may be critical while no singleton in it is.
`L299.s2` | S2 | Criticality is relative to the route \(W\) it is assessed in, a **route** of the candidate being a member of \(\mathsf S_{E,p}\) (not an active route of a history, Part IX): a commitment critical in one route need not be critical in the full candidate, and the routes assessed are subsets of the written \(\Gamma\), whether or not anyone has set them out, not a route someone could write with commitments outside \(\Gamma\).
`L299.s3` | S2 | For a declared family \(\mathcal V\) of organization edits,
`L301.s1` | FROZEN | \[ \operatorname{Boundary}_{E,p}=\{(v,w)\in\mathcal V^2:\operatorname{Account}(E_v,p)\neq\operatorname{Account}(E_w,p)\}. \tag{D} \]
`L305.s1` | S2 | **Finite monotone claim.** If \(\Gamma\) is finite, \(\mathsf S\) is upward closed, and \(\Gamma\in\mathsf S\), then \(d\in\Gamma\) is critical for some route (**contributory**) exactly when \(d\in\bigcup\min\mathsf S\), and \(d\) is **globally indispensable**, \(\Gamma\setminus\{d\}\notin\mathsf S_{E,p}\), exactly when \(d\in\bigcap\min\mathsf S\).
`L305.s2` | S2 | *Why this and not its denial.*
`L305.s3` | S2 | A member of a minimal route is critical for it.
`L305.s4` | S2 | If \(d\) is critical for \(W\), finiteness gives a minimal \(U\subseteq W\); if \(d\notin U\), upward closure makes \(W\setminus\{d\}\) a route.
`L305.s5` | S2 | Deletion of \(d\) from \(\Gamma\) leaves \(\Gamma\setminus\{d\}\) a route exactly when a minimal route omits \(d\). ∎ The claim applies only where its assumptions are met; an addition to \(\Gamma\) that stops a route being one is the interference case below, and there upward closure fails.
`L307.s1` | FROZEN | **Redundant routes.** \(\Gamma=\{a,b\}\), \(\mathsf S=\{\{a\},\{b\},\{a,b\}\}\): each is contributory, neither indispensable.
`L307.s2` | S2 | Two systems with the same output table may differ in which routes are active; the semantics represents the difference (Argument 9).
`L307.s3` | S2 | A route of the candidate is a route whether or not any history runs it; it is active in a system when occurrences that realize it form an active route (Part IX), a subnetwork of actual occurrences in the system's history.
`L307.s4` | S2 | The two meet in \(\operatorname{ProducedBy}\) (Part XI), which attributes a repair to the contributions whose active routes ran to it, not to the routes a candidate contains.
`L307.s5` | S2 | A route already present in the candidate is a route whether or not anyone has described its work; a component reassigned to a new target after a deletion belongs to a new candidate with its own assessment, and whether the new candidate meets (E) is not whether the old one does.
`L309.s1` | FROZEN | **Interference.** \(\Gamma=\{a,b\}\), \(\mathsf S=\{\{a\}\}\): the full candidate fails (E) although a subset meets it.
`L309.s2` | S2 | A subset can meet (E) while the whole fails it; \(b\) is not made "not a commitment" to repair this.
`L311.s1` | S2 | **Infinitary routes.** \(\Gamma=\{d_n:n\in\mathbb N\}\), \(d_n\) the constraint \(|x|\le 1/n\): every set of indices unbounded in \(\mathbb N\) determines \(x=0\); no minimal route, and no route of one commitment, exists.
`L311.s2` | FROZEN | (B) records the collective contribution.
`L313.s1` | S2 | **Commitments that do no work.** (E) has no condition that each commitment do work.
`L313.s2` | S2 | A commitment \(d\) of a candidate that has a route does no work by itself in it when every route stays a route after \(d\) is added to it and after \(d\) is removed from it: a candidate carrying \(d\) then meets (E) exactly when it meets (E) without \(d\), and \(\{d\}\) is critical in no route (B).
`L313.n3` | S2 | When \(\Gamma\) is infinite, a block of such commitments can still be critical (Infinitary routes; FC40 (c)).
`L315.s1` | FROZEN | **Rivals.** Two explanatory candidates for one question \(p\) are **rivals** when one of them has been offered as an answer to \(p\) in place of the other and they conflict at some admitted edit–boundary pair of the target that both their transports translate, in \(C\) or outside it.
`L315.n2` | S2 | Two candidates **conflict** at such a pair \((a,b)\) when their answers there differ (D8.2), or when each of them could meet (F1), (F2) and (A) there under some relations of the target's components at that pair, each a relation on the component's footprint (Part II), and no such relations let both, as none do when two of their active components with one counterpart have different relations there (D8.new1).
`L315.s3` | S2 | Whether two candidates conflict depends on their organizations and transports and on the target's ports and components, not on anyone's view of them; it is found by argument, with no test, and it does not turn on what any physics admits (Part I).
`L315.s4` | FROZEN | A candidate offered for \(p\) is offered for the whole of \(p\): it claims (F1), (F2) and (A) at every pair of \(C\), tested or not, and the rest of (E) on \(C\); outside \(C\) it claims nothing on \(p\), but what its organization and transport give there can conflict with what another's give.
`L315.s5` | FROZEN | Two candidates that differ only in how they are written, one carried onto the other by a structure-preserving bijection that takes its transport with it and leaves its answers as they are, conflict at no pair (Part VIII, Recoding; Argument 8), and nor do two candidates, however differently they are cut, that some such relations of the target would let both meet (F1), (F2) and (A) at each admitted pair both translate; neither pair is a pair of rivals.

588	
589	`L403.s1` | S3 | **Deployment.** \(\operatorname{Deploy}_{\beta,\ell}(s,c,\xi;U)\) is met when \(s\) at \(\xi\) holds a representation of \(c\), by (R) a faithful transport with selected or constructed provenance, integrated into problem-directed activity and serving the declared use task \(U\) as a retained capability (Part XII).

`L325.s5` | S2 | The reversed calculation \(H=L\tan\theta\) is not: intervening on \(H\) changes the target's \(L\) but not the calculation's \(L\).
`L325.n6` | S2 | It is faithful under the identification contract \(C_{\mathrm{id}}=\{1\}\times B\) (E1).
`L325.s7` | S2 | Direction is set by the admitted edits; the nouns "pole" and "shadow" fix nothing.

## Identification

`L329.s1` | S2 | Let \(Z\) be the admitted states, \(g:Z\to Y\) the measurement, \(f:Z\to F\) the feature.
`L329.s2` | S2 | The fibre at \(y\) is \(Z_y=g^{-1}(y)\).
`L329.s3` | FROZEN | The feature is identified at \(y\) exactly when \(Z_y\neq\varnothing\land|f[Z_y]|=1\).
`L329.s4` | S2 | (I1) It is identified on every attainable \(y\) exactly when \(f=\bar f\circ g\) for some \(\bar f\).
`L329.s5` | S2 | (I2) For linear \(g\) and linear feature \(c^\top\), identification is \(\ker g\subseteq\ker c^\top\).
`L329.s6` | S2 | (I3) Repeating rows changes no kernel; an independent calibration can.
`L331.s1` | S2 | For the two balances \(\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\1&0&1\end{pmatrix}\), reading an unknown mass \(x\) with biases \(b_A,b_B\), in that order, the kernel is spanned by \((1,-1,-1)\); the readings identify \(b_B-b_A\) and not \(x\).
`L331.s2` | S2 | This is an account of a limitation.
`L331.s3` | S2 | "Set \(b_B=0\) because it gives the mass I favour" is not an inference from the readings; it is circular, though the value it sets might be the target's.

## Obstruction

`L335.s1` | FROZEN | For allowed steps \(R\) and an invariant \(I\) with \(zRz'\Rightarrow I(z)=I(z')\), no allowed path joins states of different invariant value.
`L335.s2` | FROZEN | (O1) Equal values do not suffice for reachability.
`L335.s3` | S2 | Twenty-three indivisible tokens cannot be split equally three ways; permitting division changes the state space and makes a new question (Part III); the scoped result on its own question is as it was.

## Explanations that remove structure

`L339.s1` | S2 | A question of the form "why is there no \(X\)-effect?" has a target \(D\) in which the ports and components a rival account would need are absent, and a contract containing the edits that would introduce them.
`L339.s2` | S2 | An account is faithful when introducing those components changes the answer in \(E\) as it does in \(D\), and their absence leaves both unchanged.
`L339.s3` | S2 | The rival's supposed structure has as its counterpart a *deleted* subnetwork, whose relation is full (Part II).
`L339.s4` | S2 | This is the semantics' treatment of eliminative explanation; it is offered as an account, and is listed under attack (Nec) in Part XV as a place where it may not be one.
`L339.s5` | S2 | Where the absent structure appears to be present, the question why it appears is a separate question with its own target and contract (Part III): an account of the absence neither answers that question nor needs to, and a bare denial, which offers no component that responds to a change in what produces the appearance, is not an account of it.

## Odd-order skew-symmetric matrices

`L343.s1` | FROZEN | Question: why is every odd-order real skew-symmetric matrix singular?
`L343.s2` | FROZEN | Contract: remove skewness; remove oddness; remove both; field arithmetic and determinant–invertibility held fixed.
`L343.s3` | FROZEN | The full Leibniz expansion with skewness substituted meets (F1) and (F2): every intermediate product is a determinant suborganization whose hidden ports project away.
`L343.s4` | S2 | It meets (A): the answer is the absence of invertible matrices in the family, and under each contrast the family contains one.
`L343.n5` | S2 | \(\operatorname{Dependence}\) is met: \(I_3\) is an instance under removal of skewness, and \(\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}\) under removal of oddness.
`L343.s6` | S2 | Non-vacuity is met: any nonzero odd skew matrix is an instance, and the edits the target admits outside the contract, to the field arithmetic and to the link between determinant and invertibility, are left out by the stated scope.
`L343.s7` | S2 | No edit here is a physical one, and none needs to be: the contract is a set of changes to the mathematical target (Part III).
`L343.s8` | FROZEN | The expansion is an account.
`L343.s9` | S2 | That a three-line piece of mathematics is shorter is not a fifth condition.

## Constitutive rules

`L347.s1` | FROZEN | A rule relation \(C_r\subseteq Z\times S\) answers "which status under this rule?" by its fibre.
`L347.s2` | FROZEN | Its signature under (K) is invariant under interventions on \(Z\) and variable under edits to \(C_r\).
`L347.s3` | FROZEN | Whether the rule governs a practice, and whether it should, are separate questions with separate contracts.

# Part VIII — Transport results

`L353.s1` | S3 | **Functional transport.** Let \(S_a\) be a target process and \(T_a\) a represented process for each admitted generator \(a\).
`L353.s2` | S3 | If \(\pi\circ S_a=T_a\circ\pi\) for every admitted generator \(a\), the same equation is met by every admitted finite composition with matching scopes.
`L353.s3` | S3 | *Why this and not its denial.*
`L353.s4` | S3 | \(\pi S_bS_a=T_b\pi S_a=T_bT_a\pi\); induct. ∎
`L355.s1` | S3 | **Relational transport.** For \(R\subseteq Z_D\times Z_E\), forward preservation is
`L357.s1` | S3 | \[ zRy\land z\xrightarrow{a}z'\Rightarrow\exists y'[y\xrightarrow{\tau(a)}y'\land z'Ry'], \tag{T1} \]
`L361.s1` | S3 | with the backward condition required for equivalence rather than one-sided abstraction.
`L361.s2` | FROZEN | Composition of relations preserves both directions when intermediate scopes agree.
`L363.s1` | S3 | **Approximate transport.** Let \(S\) be a target next-step process and \(T\) a represented next-step process, as \(S_a\) and \(T_a\) are in functional transport, and let \(d\) be a metric on \(X_E\).
`L363.s2` | S3 | With one-step discrepancy \(d(\pi Sz,T\pi z)\le\varepsilon\) at every state \(z\) of a stated scope, and with \(T\) \(L\)-Lipschitz for \(d\), the discrepancy after \(n\) steps from one state \(z\), \(e_n=d(\pi S^nz,T^n\pi z)\) (so \(e_0=0\)), meets the bound \(e_n\le\varepsilon\sum_{k<n}L^k\) whenever \(z,Sz,\dots,S^{n-1}z\) lie in that scope.
`L363.s3` | S3 | (T2) Without a modulus, no accumulated bound follows.
`L363.s4` | S3 | An exact question is not silently replaced by an approximate one.
`L365.s1` | S3 | **Recoding.** A declared, invertible recoding of a carrier preserves the content when a reader who applies the declared convention recovers every pairing (Argument 8).
`L365.s2` | S3 | A section of a carrier filled from another source keeps that other source's history, whatever it happens to match.
`L367.s1` | S3 | **Historical index.** A proposition indexed to a contract remains that proposition when a later theory changes the current contract.
`L367.s2` | S3 | A new index is a new claim.
`L369.s1` | FROZEN | **A failed answer stays failed.** Fix a question \(p\), a pair \((a,b)\in C\) and a value \(y\neq\operatorname{Ans}_p(a,b)\).
`L369.s2` | FROZEN | By (A), a candidate for \(p\) whose answer at \((a,b)\) is \(y\), \(\operatorname{Ans}_E(\tau(a),\sigma(b))=y\), is not an account of \(p\), whether it is the candidate that gave \(y\) there and failed, that candidate offered again, a rival, or a changed candidate that keeps \(y\) there; and so on every question with the same target and query whose contract contains \((a,b)\).
`L369.s3` | S3 | Once an argument usable by an assessor rules out \(y\) as the target's answer at \((a,b)\), every such candidate alike is ruled out for that assessor, from the candidate's own answer there, with no record of which candidates failed before or of how any was changed.
`L369.s4` | S3 | Here "ruled out" is meant as in Part VI: the assessor holds an argument usable by that assessor (Part IX) that rules out the claim that \(y\) is the target's answer at \((a,b)\); joined to a candidate's own answer \(y\) there and to (A), it rules out that the candidate meets (E); and by (K3) an argument from the test that records it rules out a candidate only together with the background and instruments the test uses.
`L369.s5` | S3 | If a premise about them ceases to be live, the argument is not usable (K2) and those candidates are no longer ruled out by it, every such candidate alike; no candidate becomes an account by that (E).
`L369.s6` | S3 | A contract that omits \((a,b)\), or a changed query, makes a different question (Part III): an account on it does not answer \(p\), and it leaves the failure on \(p\) as it was (Historical index).

# Part IX — Criticism, use, and usable arguments

`L375.n1` | S3 | **Histories.** A history \(h\) is a set of occurrences with an acyclic causal precedence \(\prec_h\) (\(\preceq_h\,:=\,\prec_h^{*}\); \(\forall X\subseteq h\,[X\neq\varnothing\Rightarrow\exists x\in X\,\forall y\in X\,\neg\,y\prec_h x]\), D11.3) and a physical interpretation supplying process occurrences, their ports, and the connections actually instantiated.
`L375.s2` | FROZEN | An **active route** is a connected subnetwork of actual occurrences joining a represented input to an operative result, whose components meet the applicable relations and which has nonconstant dependence on the represented distinction under the declared contrasts.
`L375.s3` | S3 | A route that started and did no work, or that was already at rest when the result occurred, is not active for that result; whether a route is active is read from the history, not from the result.
`L377.s1` | S3 | **Bearing.** A criticism has target \(z\), alleged defect \(\delta\), premise \(g\), and a connection.
`L377.s2` | S3 | Let \(p_\delta\) be the question whether \(z\) has \(\delta\) in respect of \(p\), and \(\mathcal E_c\) the explanatory candidate (Part V) for \(p_\delta\) whose organization is the criticism's connection from \(g\) to \(\delta\), with its transport and its identified commitments.
`L377.s3` | S3 | Then
`L379.s1` | S3 | \[ \operatorname{Bearing}(c,z,p)\iff\operatorname{Account}(\mathcal E_c). \tag{K1} \]
`L383.s1` | FROZEN | A criticism occurrence can exist when (K1) fails.
`L383.s2` | S3 | An adverse signal is not a criticism until an organization represents it as the premise of a criticism alleging a defect in a target.
`L385.s1` | FROZEN | **Reason use.** A response uses a reason when a structural map from the represented objection into the response suborganization preserves role bindings, sends content-preserving recodings to the same transition, sends content changes to the changes specified by the operative deliberative rule, and lands on an active route.
`L385.s2` | S3 | Using an objection does not give it bearing (K1) or make any argument from it usable (K2).
`L387.s1` | S3 | **Usability.** For argument step \(u\) with essential premises \(\operatorname{Prem}(u)\), the premises its inference form uses:
`L389.s1` | FROZEN | \[ \operatorname{Usable}_j(u)\iff\operatorname{Form}_j(u)\land\operatorname{Scope}_j(u)\land\forall d\in\operatorname{Prem}(u),\operatorname{Live}_j(d;u). \tag{K2} \]
`L393.n1` | S3 | \(\operatorname{Form}_j(u)\): the inference form of \(u\) is one \(j\) admits.
`L393.n2` | S3 | \(\operatorname{Scope}_j(u)\): \(u\) is applied within the contract, grain and boundary \(j\) has declared for it; \(\operatorname{Live}_j(d;u)\): \(d=\operatorname{concl}(u')\) for some \(u'\in\operatorname{Below}(u)\) with \(\operatorname{Usable}_j(u')\) (D9.4), or a premise \(j\) tentatively accepts, having taken it up, for whatever reason, and not withdrawn it, whether or not \(j\) holds an explanation of \(d\); a claim \(j\) has never taken up is not live for \(j\).
`L393.s3` | S3 | Admitting a form, like accepting a claim, is tentative (Part 0).
`L393.n4` | S3 | For \(d\in\operatorname{Prem}(u)\): \(d\notin\operatorname{Accepted}_j(\xi')\land\neg\exists u'\in\operatorname{Below}(u)\,[\operatorname{concl}(u')=d\land\operatorname{Usable}^{\xi'}_j(u')]\Rightarrow\neg\operatorname{Usable}^{\xi'}_j(u)\); and \(\operatorname{Accepted}_j(\xi')\subseteq\operatorname{Accepted}_j(\xi)\), \(\operatorname{Forms}_j\), \(\operatorname{Scope}_j\) fixed \(\Rightarrow X^{\xi'}_j(\psi)\subseteq X^{\xi}_j(\psi)\) (D9.4, D9.8, FC70, FC56).
`L395.n1` | S3 | **What a test rules out.** For \(T\land B\land I\Rightarrow O:\ \alpha\in X_j(O)\land\operatorname{Usable}_j(u^{+})\land\forall l\in\operatorname{leaves}(\alpha)\,[\neg(T\land B\land I)\notin\operatorname{conj}(l)\land\neg\operatorname{MadeFrom}(l,\neg(T\land B\land I))]\Rightarrow\alpha^{+}\in X_j(T\land B\land I);\quad\forall x\in\{T,B,I\}:\neg\operatorname{RO}(\alpha^{+},x)\) (D9.9). (K3)
`L397.s1` | S3 | **Arguments.** A record leaf is a reference to an event with an interpreted claim.
`L397.n2` | S3 | An argument is an argument tree (D9.2) whose leaves are premises, which are record leaves or stated assumptions and definitions.
`L397.s3` | S3 | Each step of an argument rules out the case in which the step's premises are met and its conclusion fails, for someone who admits its inference form (\(\operatorname{Form}_j\)), while that form stays admitted.
`L397.n4` | S3 | An argument \(\alpha\) is usable by \(j\) when \(\forall u\in\operatorname{steps}(\alpha)\ \operatorname{Usable}_j(u)\land[\operatorname{steps}(\alpha)=\varnothing\Rightarrow\operatorname{concl}(\alpha)\in\operatorname{Accepted}_j(\xi)]\) (D9.6), and it rules out a claim when the claim is inconsistent with its conclusion and the claim's denial is not among its premises (below).
`L397.s5` | FROZEN | For \(\psi\), \(X_j(\psi)\) is the set of arguments usable by \(j\) that rule out \(\psi\).
`L397.s6` | S3 | Where no argument usable by \(j\) rules out \(\phi\), that absence rules out nothing, neither \(\phi\) nor \(\neg\phi\).
`L397.n7` | S3 | An argument need not cite a test: one with no record leaf that finds, by examining a candidate, that it gives what a claim excludes (Part VI, conflict with a claim), rules the candidate out for whoever can use it, on a question about the world as on any other.
`L397.n8` | S3 | Where such an argument uses a claim taken as given, the ruling out is a choice the person using it made, not something the claim does by itself (Part 0).
`L397.s9` | S3 | **Premises taken as given.** A premise may be a claim taken as given: tentatively accepted, for whatever reason, even with no thought given to it, by someone who holds no explanation of it.
`L397.s10` | S3 | As to its premises, (K2) asks only that they be live for the person using the step; neither it nor anything else in the semantics asks that the person represent (R) a premise's explanation, or any part of it, before using the premise to find an error.
`L397.n11` | S3 | That a person can use a claim so, without containing its explanation, is a costly gamble for all creative agents; and if this were not possible, error correction could become impossibly costly to perform.
`L397.s12` | S3 | The semantics names the gamble and puts no measure on it.
`L397.s13` | FROZEN | A system can be designed that must hold the whole explanation of a premise before using it; that is a detail outside the process the semantics describes, and the semantics does not require it.
`L397.n14` | S3 | **A premise that is the denial.** An argument does not rule out a claim when the claim's denial is among its premises, alone or joined to other claims by "and", read structurally (D9.7) and not by logical equivalence alone; nor does an argument whose record leaf was made from a claim rule out that claim's denial.
`L397.s16` | S3 | Such an argument, as one against that claim, has its conclusion among its premises, as in "\(p\) because \(p\)", and does not rule that claim out for anyone.
`L397.s17` | S3 | A person may still drop the claim, for whatever reason (Part 0): that is the person's choice, not a ruling out, and it leaves the claim not ruled out and any problem it poses as it was (Part VI).
`L397.n17` | S3 | A premise taken as given differs from such a premise: it finds that the candidate gives what the premise excludes.
`L397.s19` | S3 | The block catches only a premise that is the claim's denial, read structurally; a premise from which a step leads to the denial, as one does from \(r\) and "if \(r\), this candidate fails (E)", is a premise taken as given, and using it is the gamble above, not a circular argument.
`L397.s20` | S3 | Where the premises \(j\) tentatively accepts are inconsistent, arguments from them can rule out, for \(j\), a claim and its denial alike; the semantics then says only that \(j\)'s premises conflict, and which of them \(j\) drops, if any, is \(j\)'s choice (Part 0).

# Part X — Understanding, construction, and origin

`L403.s1` | S3 | **Deployment.** \(\operatorname{Deploy}_{\beta,\ell}(s,c,\xi;U)\) is met when \(s\) at \(\xi\) holds a representation of \(c\), by (R) a faithful transport with selected or constructed provenance, integrated into problem-directed activity and serving the declared use task \(U\) as a retained capability (Part XII).
`L403.s2` | FROZEN | The repertoire \(R_{\beta,\ell}(s,\xi)\) is the set of contents deployable in some nontrivial use respect.
`L403.s3` | FROZEN | A system may understand a theory in error.
`L403.s4` | S3 | A narrow retained use is what it is: it suffices neither for the wider understanding it falls short of nor for a permanent inability to reach it.
`L405.n1` | S3 | **Construction.** \(\operatorname{Build}_{\beta,\ell}(s,c,h,e)\) is met when an actual subhistory owned by \(s\) and delimited at \(e\) prepares \(\operatorname{Held}_\ell(o,c)\) (D13.3, D18.1) for explanatory use of \(c\), contains a nontrivial binding construction relevant to that use, and is not a composition of content-preserving transfers.

# S107 Round 4 — formal claims, after round 4

The claims the merge touches were run singly on the merged program (`integration notes.md` §9); the whole suite is the harness job `r4 claim suite, merged` (key after_round4 of the json). Sources, quotations, parts: `formal claims, after round 4.json`. Column r4: 'restated' = the statement changed (S106's kept in the json as formal_after_s106); 'note' = the code or its print changed, the statement kept; 'new' = a test claim of round 4 (not a move). H holds on all models tried; CEX counterexample found; NT not tested. Built by `build formal claims after round 4.py`; then the second checker on the critical review (`results/S107 Round 4 - the second checker on the critical review.md`) changed five claims in place (column r4: 'second check (On)'; the json keeps each earlier title and statement as title_before_r4b, formal_before_r4b).*

**Counts.** After S106: 128 H, 2 CEX, 7 NT of 137. **After round 4 (expected): 133 H, 2 CEX, 7 NT of 142** (137 + 5 new, each H; no status of an earlier claim changed; test parts FC84.new1 (a3), FC30.new1 (h) added, each as claimed). **After the second check: 133 H, 2 CEX, 7 NT of 142** (whole suite rerun; statuses unchanged; FC84.new1 (a4) and FC83's look added, each as expected; FC84.new1 (a3), FC27.new1, FC72.new2 (b), (d) and FC83 restated).     """Round 3's NonCircular: NC0 ∧ NC1 ∧ NC2 (D6.5 after round 3, I25); NC0 holds of every candidate (D6.2, I23).

def dep(cand):
    """Dep(ℰ) :⟺ NC0 ∧ NC2 (D6.5 after S106; I24's other choice (a), I25's 'NC2 alone'). NC0 holds of every
    candidate (D6.2, I23), so Dep is NC2: some contrast of E's answers at a pair of C is lost when a nonempty

def nonvacuous(cand):
    p = cand.p
    allpairs = frozenset((a, b) for a in p.D.A for b in p.D.B)
    return bool(p.D.sol(ONE, p.b0)) and (allpairs - p.C) <= p.excl

def account(cand, detail=False, reading=None):
    """Acc(ℰ) (E) (D6.7). With detail, the value of each conjunct. After S106 the conjuncts are F1, F2, A, Dep
    (= NC2, NC0 holding of every candidate) and NonVacuous; NC1 (no answer slot, D6.3) is still computed and
    reported in the detail, as content criticism can point at (D6.3), and is not a conjunct. reading "r3":
    round 3's (E), NC1 a conjunct."""
    reading = reading or ACCOUNT_READING
    d = {}
    d["translates C"] = translated_C(cand)
    if not d["translates C"]:
        d.update({"F1": False, "F2": False, "A": False, "NC1": False, "NC2": False, "Dep": False, "NonVacuous": nonvacuous(cand)})
    else:
        d["F1"] = F1(cand)
        d["F2eq"] = F2eq(cand)
        d["Hom"] = hom(cand)
        d["F2"] = d["F2eq"] and d["Hom"]

    keys = ("F1", "F2", "A", "NC1", "NC2", "NonVacuous") if reading == "r3" else ("F1", "F2", "A", "Dep", "NonVacuous")
    val = all(d[k] for k in keys)
    return (val, d) if detail else val

# Part A, section 2 (transports, provenance, account, conflict) — report

Baseline commands run: `--claim FC26 --claim FC27 --claim FC22 --claim FC23`, `--claim FC25.new2 --claim FC30.new1 --claim FC44 --claim FC52`, `--claim FC28 --claim FC40`, `--claim FC23.new2 --claim FC72.new2` (all at default scale/time). All results quoted below are from these runs; everything "after" is **not run**.

## (a) The variants

| id | item(s) varied | old → new | kind | why chosen | departs from |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V2.1 | D6.4 (NC2), L255.n2 | NC2(ℰ) :⟺ ∃(a,b)∈C: Contrast(E; x) — the Lost clause and the block G deleted | weaken | severs the only conjunct of (E) that ties the answer to Γ | none |
| V2.2 | D6.4 (NC2) | G restricted: ∃d∈Γ: Contrast(E;x) ∧ Lost(E,{d};x) | strengthen | ties Dependence to one-commitment work; collective blocks stop witnessing | none |
| V2.3 | D6.4 (NC2) | witness pair required a ≠ 1 (∈ C, a ≠ 1) | strengthen | makes Dependence read edits only; boundary-only contrasts stop counting | none |
| V2.4 | D6.7 ((E)), L261.n1 | Acc(ℰ) :⟺ F1 ∧ F2 ∧ A ∧ NC0 ∧ **NC1** ∧ NC2 ∧ NonVacuous | strengthen | puts the written-in test back as a conjunct | rejected by S45 ("Yes, take the test out"), with S44 |
| V2.5 | D12.1 (Sel), L195 | "H ⊆ C finite and nonempty" → "H ⊆ C finite" (I52's other choice) | weaken | with H = ∅ a stipulated population makes any transport Sel | departs in effect from S41 Q2 ("No, not if just declared") |
| V2.6 | D8.2 (Conf), L315.n2 | "For (a,b) ∈ A_D × B_D … in C or outside it" → "For (a,b) ∈ C" | weaken | confines conflict to the contract | blocks FROZEN L315.s1, L317.s6; departs in effect from S20 ("If two discovered variations fit, that constitutes a problem") |
| V2.7 | D8.5 (ConfCl), L315.n11 | ConfCl(ℰ,χ;a,b) :⟺ [∃R Ans^R_p(a,b)=y ∧ ∀R(Ans^R_p(a,b)=y ⇒ R ∉ Allow_χ(a,b))] (second disjunct deleted) | weaken | a claim conflicts only through the candidate's answer, never through the relations it needs | rejected by S27 (perpetual motion enough to trigger a conflict) |
| V2.8 | D9.8 (Out), L315.s6–s7 | Out_j('Acc(ℰ)') :⟺ ∃α ∈ X_j('Acc(ℰ)') with **Acc(ℰ) ∈ Uses(α)** (I196's instance reading) | swap | changes which arguments rule a candidate out, hence (Suff)'s defeat set | none |

## (b) The traces

**V2.1 — Dependence without loss.** Case (program notation, not run): D with ports x,y,z ∈ {0,1}; comps cx:(x), cy:(x,y), dz:(z); B = {b0}; A = {1,e}, e·e = undef; L_cx(1,b0) = full, L_cx(e,b0) = {(1)}; L_cy(·,b0) = {(0,0),(1,1)}; L_dz full at both pairs. p: Q_w reads y, δ_D = y, C = {(1,b0),(e,b0)}. ℰ = D with the identity transport, Γ = {dz}, λ(dz) = ({dz}, z:=id(z)); δ_E = y. Before: F1 ✓, F2 ✓, A ✓, NonVacuous ✓ (Sol_D(1,b0) = {(0,0,*),(1,1,*)}); Ans_p(1,b0) = ⊥, Ans_p(e,b0) = 1; the only block of Γ is {dz}, and E−{dz} answers the same → ¬Lost → ¬NC2 → ¬Acc. After V2.1: Contrast at (e,b0) holds → Acc(ℰ) = True (still not an explanation: identity transport declared). Newly meeting (E): every candidate all of whose commitments do no work (L313's case) whose answers vary over C — the written-in and the idle-commitment candidate alike. Which stop: none.

**V2.2 — singleton block.** Case: L311's infinitary Γ = {d_n : n ∈ ℕ}, d_n the constraint |x| ≤ 1/n (FC40 run: routes = unbounded index sets, every critical block infinite, no one-commitment route). Before: NC2 witnessed by any unbounded G (deleting it frees x; contrast x = 0 vs free lost) — not run as NC2, derivation from D6.4; the candidate meets the rest of (E) as FC72.new2 (a) does for its own. After V2.2: deleting one d_n leaves sup 1/m = 0 over the rest → contrast stays → ¬Dependence → the infinitary candidate stops meeting (E), stops being an explanation. Also L307's redundant candidate (Γ = {a,b}, each alone a route, FROZEN L307.s1): before, G = {a,b} witnesses NC2 → meets (E); after, no singleton loses the contrast → stops meeting (E). Newly counting: none.

**V2.3 — witness needs an edit.** Case: the reversed calculation on the identification contract (FC28 run: on C_id = {1}×B, E_rev meets (F1), (F2), (A) on all 9 boundaries, answers {u_H} vary). Before: NC2 witnessed at (1,b), b ≠ b0, contrast {1} vs {2}, lost by G = {r_L} (L freed → (T,L) not single → ⊥ where determined) — NC2 derivation not run; so E_rev meets (E) on C_id. After V2.3: every pair of C_id has a = 1 → no witness → ¬Dependence → E_rev stops meeting (E) on C_id; and so does E_fwd (identity) on C_id, and every candidate on every contract of the form {1}×B: identification questions (E2, L329) admit no accounts at all.
